title: Harness circuit-breaker for repeated identical BLOCKED_AMBIGUITY on the same story ID
description:
Problem: CAM-92's PRD had self-contradictory acceptance criteria (AC1-3 dedup collapses the formatWorkerReportSummary( call-site count in loop.ts to 1, while a pre-existing CAM-94 static-grep test "AC7" pins it at 3, and AC4 forbade touching existing supervisor tests). The sidecar re-dispatched the SAME single story across 10 consecutive fresh implementer sessions, each hitting the identical deterministic contradiction and returning BLOCKED_AMBIGUITY, before an operator amended the PRD. ~10 sessions of ~10-15k output tokens each with zero PRD-side progress = pure waste.

Ask: add a harness-level circuit breaker that detects repeated identical terminal-blocked outcomes (same storyId + same outcome.kind + unchanged PRD) across N consecutive sessions and halts the auto-dispatch loop, surfacing a durable escalation marker to the orchestrator (mirroring .cam-plan-escalated.json) instead of re-spinning. Suggested: threshold N=2 or 3; key on (storyId, outcome.kind, prd content hash) so a real PRD amendment resets the counter. Out of scope: fixing any specific PRD (that is an operator/planner amendment).

acceptanceCriteria: On every blocked terminal, the harness computes a dedup key (storyId, specific BLOCKED_* token, sha256 of prd.json). The specific token is read from CAM-195's blocked-terminal marker/reason (the collapsed WorkerOutcomeKind 'blocked' is insufficient); the sha256 of prd.json is net-new (no PRD content hash exists today).

A cross-session consecutive-blocked counter is persisted by extending CAM-195's .cam-implement-blocked.json marker with { consecutiveCount, keyHash }: a blocked terminal whose key matches the stored keyHash increments consecutiveCount; a differing key (PRD amended, different story, different token) resets consecutiveCount to 1 and rewrites keyHash.

Threshold N=3: on the third consecutive identical blocked outcome the circuit breaker halts the auto-dispatch chain, i.e. it does NOT call flipActiveFn at the re-dispatch decision point (src/supervisor/loop.ts:2053-2056) and the loop stays active:false instead of re-spinning a fresh implementer against the same deterministic contradiction.

On halt the marker is flagged escalated:true (with a haltedAt timestamp); the orchestrator boot-read surfaces a distinct circuit-broken blocker line (e.g. '⚠ implement circuit-broken: <issue> story=<id> (<N> identical BLOCKED_...) — needs PRD amendment'), read-only, never deleting the marker.

Recovery: a PRD amendment changes sha256(prd.json) so the next blocked terminal resets consecutiveCount and clears escalated, re-enabling the auto-chain; a DONE outcome clears the marker via CAM-195's consume path. The counter never stays stuck across a real amendment.
spec.scope: Add a harness-level circuit breaker that bounds the CAM-92 failure mode: the sidecar auto-dispatch chain re-dispatched the SAME single story across ~10 fresh implementer sessions, each hitting the identical deterministic BLOCKED_AMBIGUITY contradiction (~10-15k output tokens each, zero PRD progress) before an operator amended the PRD. Detect N consecutive identical terminal-blocked outcomes keyed on (storyId, BLOCKED_* token, PRD content hash) and halt the auto-chain, surfacing a durable escalation via CAM-195's .cam-implement-blocked.json marker instead of re-spinning. Builds ON CAM-195: shares the finishTerminal seam (loop.ts:749-752) and the re-dispatch decision point (loop.ts:2053-2056), and extends CAM-195's marker rather than creating a parallel counter file. Out of scope: fixing any specific PRD (that is an operator/planner amendment); the counter only halts and escalates.
gotchas: blockedBy CAM-195: the two features land on the same two seams (finishTerminal, the flipActiveFn auto-chain) and CAM-214 extends CAM-195's .cam-implement-blocked.json marker schema. CAM-195 must land first; do not build in parallel against these shared seams.

The auto-chain re-dispatch (loop.ts:2053-2056) only fires when flipActiveFn is injected (plan_approval==='auto'); in default/ci-gated modes the loop pauses for a human cam next, so the runaway (and thus the breaker) is auto-mode-specific. The breaker must not change the default/ci-gated pause behavior.

The specific BLOCKED_* token (BLOCKED_AMBIGUITY vs BLOCKED_QUALITY) survives only in worker-report.json / outcome.detail today, not in the collapsed 'blocked' WorkerOutcomeKind recorded in the event log; the key must source the token from the marker CAM-195 populates, not from the event-log result stream.

The escalated circuit-broken surfacing text lives in the orchestrator boot-read prose in templates/agents/subagent-orchestrator.md (and embedded copy); editing templates/ requires bun run embed-vendor + embed-vendor:check. This adds only the escalated:true branch to the boot-read that CAM-195 introduces.
sha256(prd.json) is net-new hashing; no PRD content hash exists in the codebase today (existing createHash uses are the tmux session name and the SUGGESTION-fingerprint dedup, both unrelated).
